content.text: The excerpt reviews diseases of the mouth, tongue, tonsils, pharynx, oesophagus, and functional dyspepsia. It describes causes, symptoms, pathology, diagnosis, prognosis, complications, and historical treatments for mercurial stomatitis, glossitis, macroglossia, ulcers, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, oesophagitis, strictures, carcinoma, paralysis, and dilatation. Severe conditions may cause gangrene, hemorrhage, airway obstruction, malnutrition, or death. Management emphasizes removing causes, hygiene, antiseptic or soothing applications, nutrition, supportive care, and surgery when abscesses, obstruction, necrosis, or deformity occur. For superficial pharyngitis, the patient should rest in bed or on a lounge. Functional dyspepsia is linked mainly to nervous exhaustion, poor diet, overeating, constipation, and impaired gastric secretion; treatment centers on diet, exercise, rest, and addressing underlying disease.
